The Engineering Notebook is a record of your thinking. At a competition the judges don't just look at the robot; they want to know what problem you hit, what ideas you considered, why you chose what you chose, how the tests went and how you improved it.

Think of it as "the robot's diary plus a science lab report". Every decision about the robot needs a reason you can point to.

Benefits of the habit: ① you won't forget what you changed; ② teammates can follow it; ③ judges can tell you really understand; ④ it becomes your future portfolio.

70cf57|
  1. Define the problem: what are you solving? What counts as success?
  2. Brainstorm: come up with at least 3 ways, without criticizing yet.
  3. Select a solution: compare with a decision matrix and write down your reasons.
  4. Prototype: first make a simple version you can test.
  5. Test: test repeatedly and record data.
  6. Improve / Iterate: change things based on the data and return to step 4.
This is a cycle, not a one-time thing. Each time around, the robot gets better.
e3f2f4|3. Six elements of a good notebook page

a9e7bf|
  1. Date and name: on every page, so it's clear who did it and when.
  2. Goal: what is this page solving?
  3. Pictures: sketches, photos, screenshots, with labels (sizes, part names).
  4. Reasons: why did you decide this? (the most important!)
  5. Data / results: how many tests and what the results were.
  6. Next step: based on the results, what to do next.
e9e4fb|4. Decision matrix: how to compare options

f5d04a|

You have 3 claw designs. How do you choose? List the criteria, give each criterion an importance (weight), then score each option.

CriterionWeightOption A two-fingerOption B one-fingerOption C suction
Grips well3432
Fast2343
Easy to build1342
Total (score × weight)212114

Total = 4×3 + 3×2 + 3×1 = 21 (A). What if A and B tie? Look back at which criterion matters most, or test a prototype. The point is to write down the reasons.
794877|5. Test records: change only one variable at a time

57ae82|

To find out whether "speed" affects accuracy, change only the speed and keep everything else (battery level, start position, floor) the same, and test several times.

TrialSpeedTarget distanceActual distanceError
150%1000 mm990 mm−10
250%1000 mm995 mm−5
3100%1000 mm1040 mm+40

A conclusion needs evidence: "At 100% speed the error grows (+40), probably from inertia when stopping. Next step: stop 30 mm early at 100% and test 3 more times."
efa40d|6. Good notes vs. poor notes

155644|
❌ Poor

"Changed the arm today. It's better."

Where was it changed? How? How much better? Why? None of that can be told.
✅ Good

11/23 Goal: the arm wobbles when lifting the ball. Tested 5 times; the ball dropped 3 times. Guess: it's fixed with only one pin. Changed to two fixing points plus a diagonal brace. Tested 5 more times; dropped 0 times.

It has the date, goal, data, cause, fix and result.

Get comfortable writing in your own language first, then add English gradually. You'll use these sentences in judge interviews too.
